If these are not used at multiple places, better to just put the values inline instead of global constexpr variable.

Done. Removed global constexpr variables, interface name strings are now inline.

See PS4:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/4/src/nvidia-gpu/NvidiaGpuDevice.cpp#84

Let's not duplicate logic to fetch these properties since we already have it in the Inventory file. Let's implement fetch of these properties in that file only and if you want to add GPU specific behaviour create the dbus interfaces and associations conditionally based on device type GPU in the Inventory file.

Done. Removed ChassisAssembly class and all duplicate fetch logic. Assembly properties are now fetched via the existing Inventory pipeline only.

See PS3..4:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/3..4
Why do we need two sub-assemblies for each GPU? Does this mean, we will have two redfish sub-assembly resources per GPU?

Yes, the Umbriel mockup defines two sub-assemblies per GPU chassis — GPU Device Assembly (Assemblies/0) with Model, PartNumber, SerialNumber, Vendor, ProductionDate, and GPU Board Assembly (Assemblies/1) with PartNumber and Vendor only.

See mockup: mockup/nvidia-hgx-umbriel-baseboard/redfish/v1/Chassis/HGX_GPU_SXM_1/Assembly/index.json
Why is this switch case needed? Why can't these property be part of the switch case that already exists above?

Done. Removed the separate switch. Assembly property writes are now in the existing string property case.

See PS4..5:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/4..5/src/nvidia-gpu/Inventory.cpp

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/4..5/src/nvidia-gpu/NvidiaGpuAssembly.cpp

See PS4..5:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/4..5/src/nvidia-gpu/NvidiaGpuAssembly.hpp
Can we update `properties` to hold multiple interfaces? If statement after this switch statement would update value of all the interfaces.
Use sdbusplus::object_path instead.
use sdbusplus::object_path operator /.

Done in PS8. Refactored PropertyInfo to hold a list of (interface, property name) targets so one propertyId can be written to multiple D-Bus interfaces. Added addPropertyTarget helper; the if/else block after the switch is removed; the response handler iterates targets instead of branching on propertyId.

The constructor registers the assembly asset interfaces as additional targets for SERIAL_NUMBER, MARKETING_NAME, DEVICE_PART_NUMBER, and BOARD_PART_NUMBER.

Since this refactor modifies shared inventory code that predates this patch, verified on nvl32-obmc hardware that UUID, BoostClockFrequency, Power.Cap, SerialNumber, Model, and Version read byte-for-byte identical values before and after the refactor.

PS8 references:
- PropertyInfo struct: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/8/src/nvidia-gpu/Inventory.hpp#42
- addPropertyTarget helper: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/8/src/nvidia-gpu/Inventory.cpp#138
- for-loop replacing if/else: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/88572/8/src/nvidia-gpu/Inventory.cpp#366
